claim: Let \(w=(w_n)_{n\ge0}\) be a bounded sequence of positive real numbers, let \(T_w e_n=e_{n+1}w_n\) on the right quaternionic Hilbert space \(\ell^2(\mathbb H)\), and let \(r_0,r_1,\ldots>0\). Define \(T^{(0)}=T_w\) and \(T^{(k+1)}=S_{r_k}(T^{(k)})\), where \(S_r(A)=V|A|^rV\) for the polar decomposition \(A=V|A|\). If \(R_0=1\) and \(R_k=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}r_j\), then for every \(k,n\ge0\), \[T^{(k)}e_n=e_{n+2^k}w_{n+2^k-1}^{R_k}.\] Consequently, for every \(p>0\), \(T^{(k)}\) is \(p\)-hyponormal if and only if \[w_m\le w_{m+2^k}\qquad\text{for every }m\ge2^k-1.\] Thus the set of hyponormal iterates is independent of \(p\) and of the exponent schedule \(r_0,r_1,\ldots\), and it is either empty or a tail \(\{k\ge q\}\). Every \(q\in\mathbb N_0\) occurs for a bounded positive weight sequence, and the empty case also occurs.
scientific_limitations: Restricted to unilateral weighted shifts with strictly positive real weights on a right quaternionic Hilbert space.
Does not classify transforms with zero or noncentral quaternionic weights, bilateral shifts, or general operators.
An older equivalent formulation under different transform terminology remains a residual literature risk despite targeted database and primary-text searches.
title: Exact hyponormalization thresholds for iterated \(S_r\)-transforms of quaternionic weighted shifts
